rows.label: Concept
rows.text: A transformer passes energy by changing flux, with the voltage ratio equal to the turns ratio. Copper loss heats the windings in proportion to the square of the current, and core loss heats the iron whenever the flux alternates. Efficiency is output power divided by input power.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: An open secondary still has core loss.  ·  Oil-filled large transformers carry heat away. The principle is unchanged.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: A transformer has a primary coil and a secondary coil on an iron core. Alternating current in the primary changes the flux, and that changing flux induces the secondary emf. Direct current does not keep the flux changing, so a transformer does not pass steady DC.  ·  The voltage ratio equals the turns ratio when leakage is ignored. More secondary turns raise the voltage and, in the ideal case, lower the current so that input power equals output power.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Changing flux links the two coils.  ·  Step-up and step-down refer to voltage.  ·  Copper loss is I squared R in the windings.  ·  Core loss is eddy current plus hysteresis.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: A step-up transformer raises voltage. A step-down transformer lowers it. The names refer to voltage, not to power and not to current.  ·  Copper loss is the heating I squared R in both windings. It grows with the load current. Core loss is eddy-current heating plus hysteresis, and it is present whenever the flux is alternating, even if the secondary is open.  ·  Laminating the core and using soft iron cut those core losses. The efficiency is useful output power divided by input power. It is less than 1 once either loss is present.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Efficiency is not the turns ratio.  ·  Step-up does not increase power.  ·  Core loss remains on no load. Copper loss does not.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Laminations reduce eddy currents. They do not change the turns ratio.  ·  State ideal before equating the two powers.  ·  Quote efficiency as a ratio or a percentage, and say which.
